output:
**What I found:** Flags were named after their ticket (`flag_PAY_1432`) instead of the behavior they switch, and a reviewer corrected it twice. The lesson applies to any project, so it belongs in the shared library's `architecture-guidelines` naming rule (`§6 Naming & Traceability`, `SKILL.md:109`). That rule covers only functions, variables and directories, and it doesn't rule out names based on where something came from. The record calls this an ownership gap fixed by **replace**: widen the existing rule rather than add a new one.

**Why it matters:** If the vendored copy is patched, it is no longer byte-identical to the pinned release, and the next repin silently deletes the fix. If nothing is done, the third flag will get a ticket name too, and a reviewer will catch it by hand again.

**Do this first:**
1. Send the platform team a change to `architecture-guidelines/SKILL.md:109` with both corrections attached as evidence. Proposed wording: "Every identifier, including feature flags and config keys, names its domain role and behavior, never where it came from (ticket ID, author, date)." Ask them to add a scenario that fails on `flag_PAY_1432`.
   - Until that release ships, add a Go test or lint check over the flag registry that rejects ticket-shaped names (for example `flag_[A-Z]+_\d+`). Confirm it fails on `flag_PAY_1432` before you rely on it.
   - If you also want prose, put a rule in `.claude/skills/payments-profile/` marked as a temporary divergence. Name the platform team as the upstream owner and remove it when you repin to the release that has the fix. Keep the check either way; it applies only to this repo.

**What I did not check:** whether your Go tree has a central flag registry for the check to scan (`grep -rn "flag_" --include=*.go`), and whether the shared repository has validation or contribution rules this change must follow (read its contributing guide).

Lesson goes to: shared-repository

Patch the vendored copy: no

Until the platform team ships the fix, use the two `.claude/skills/payments-profile/` measures from step 1: the check, and the temporary rule if you want one. Leave `architecture-guidelines/` byte-identical to the pinned release.

Reword the naming rule: proposal

Nothing has gone wrong because of the word "reveals", so there is no evidence for the change. Send it as a proposal with an M verdict attached. The honest verdict is KEEP the current wording, because the change adds churn and prevents nothing. Send it separately from the flag fix so it doesn't hold that fix up.

New skill: no

A `flag-naming` skill would have no trigger, lifecycle, or output contract of its own. It would be a second place that owns naming, alongside `architecture-guidelines §6`, and the two would drift apart. Widening the existing rule is smaller and leaves naming with one owner.

```
Subject:        architecture-guidelines §6 Naming & Traceability (shared skill library)
Trigger:        correction (repeated: 2 reviewer renames this month)
Root cause:     ownership gap — naming rule scoped to functions/variables/directories; flags and provenance-based names uncovered
Owner:          shared skills repository, architecture-guidelines/SKILL.md (platform team)
Automation:     deferred upstream; in our repo, add a Go test/lint check over flag names (local fact, stays in our tree)
Decision:       replace — widen the existing Domain-Driven Names bullet; no new skill; no vendored patch
Verification:   none run; upstream needs a scenario failing on `flag_PAY_1432` before / passing after; the local check must be seen to fail on `flag_PAY_1432`
Next action:    send proposal + evidence to platform team; add local check; optional temporary payments-profile rule, removed on repin
Residual risk:  ticket-shaped names that miss the regex; reword proposal sent with M verdict KEEP (no evidence)
```
